title: RECONNECT THE ARCHIVE
prompt: The terminal asks for the safe route for hazardous waste. Put the steps in order.
steps: Spot the hazard and keep back
Seal it in a safe container
explanation: Spot, protect, contain, hand over. Skipping a step is how people get hurt.

title: UNLOCK THE MUNICIPAL RECORDS
prompt: The records are locked behind the waste hierarchy. Put it in order, best first.
steps: Dispose safely as a last resort
explanation: The best waste is the waste never made. Disposal comes last, not first.

title: START THE TREATMENT CYCLE
prompt: Water must pass through the stages in the right order. Set the chain.
steps: Pass it through the sand and charcoal filter
explanation: Each stage does one job: debris, sediment, fine particles, germs. Then a test proves it, because clear water is not always safe.

title: WAKE THE SOIL
prompt: Build the compost the way Jory does. Put the layers in order, bottom first.
steps: Coarse twigs for air at the bottom
A layer of browns: dry leaves and cardboard
A layer of greens: food scraps
Water it until it is damp, not wet
explanation: Air, browns, greens, water, time. Balance makes soil; plastic or batteries would poison it.

title: BALANCE THE GRID
prompt: The plant can only power so much. Put the steps to a working grid in order.
steps: Swap old motors for efficient ones
Share the rest along the line
explanation: Efficiency first: the cheapest energy is the energy you don't use. Then make clean power and keep what you can't use yet.

title: REBUILD THE ARCHIVE
prompt: Six fragments, one per region. Put the story of the collapse in order.
steps: Buy, use, discard: the loop was never closed
Action was postponed again, for good reasons each time
Cheap goods, poisoned rivers, someone else paying
Everyone waited for someone else to move first
explanation: There was no single catastrophe. The world had the solutions and kept choosing not to use them.

title: TOBI'S RADIO
prompt: An old handshake: the radio blinks a pattern. Answer it, light for light.
explanation: Radios once shared warnings between towns. A signal only works if someone answers.

title: THE FUSE BOX
prompt: Turn the burnt-out links until every bulb is wired to the supply.
explanation: Repairing a circuit costs a few minutes. Replacing the whole box costs mines, factories and trucks.

title: THE SIGNAL BOX
prompt: The signal box wants the old start-up sequence. Watch the lamps, then repeat them.
explanation: Every system has a start-up order. Learn it, and the whole line wakes up.

clue: Osei's ledger: Halden's girl's birthday, 14 July. 1-4-7.
no_clue: A three-digit dial. Halden would never write the code down here... but he might have trusted someone with it.
title: HALDEN'S SAFE
prompt: Three dials. Up and down to turn, left and right to choose.
explanation: Some things are worth locking away. Most things are worth sharing.

title: HAZARD BOARD
prompt: Match each warning to what it means.
explanation: Hazard symbols are a language. Reading it is how people stay alive around chemicals.

title: THE SORTING LINE
prompt: Knock each item into its bin (1-4) before the shredder takes it.
explanation: Sorting at the source is fast and cheap. Sorting a mountain later is neither.

title: THE PICKERS' BOARD
prompt: Match each find to where the pickers send it.
explanation: Everything has a right place. The pickers learned it by heart.

title: THE PUMP VALVES
prompt: Turn the pipe joints until water reaches every tap.
explanation: Clean water is a network: one broken joint and nobody downstream drinks.

title: THE FILTER BARREL
prompt: Layer the barrel so dirty river water drips out clear.

rules.fail: Without gravel at the bottom the sand washes straight out.
Too little sand: grit and mud get through.
Two or three layers of charcoal: enough to take out tastes and chemicals, not so much it clogs.

explanation: A filter clears dirt and some chemicals. It does not kill germs: boil it, or use the sun, too.

title: THE COMPOST HEAP
prompt: Mix a heap that will turn to soil, not slime.

rules.fail: Too many greens: it will rot and stink. More dry browns.
All browns, nothing to feed the microbes. Add some greens.
Damp like a wrung-out sponge: not dry, not soaked.
A handful of old soil brings the microbes in.

explanation: Two or three parts dry browns to one part wet greens, damp, with a little living soil: that is how waste becomes soil.

title: JORY'S SEED CHART
prompt: Match each part of the garden to what it does.
explanation: A garden is a team. Nothing in it works alone.

no_clue: Four digits. The sign says to ask the robot. There is a robot in the Forgotten Industry.
title: THE STALL PADLOCK
prompt: Four dials. Up and down to turn, left and right to choose.
explanation: Unit-7 never forgets. Machines remember what we write down.

title: UNIT-7 DIAGNOSTIC
prompt: Unit-7 blinks a test pattern and waits, patiently. Very patiently.
explanation: Maintenance is boring, constant, and the only reason anything still works.

title: THE LIFT POWER
prompt: Reconnect the lift's control lines, every lamp lit.
explanation: Mining is a last resort. Every metal you recycle is a hole you did not have to dig.

clue: Tobi, quietly: 'The sixth of December. The day I met her.' 0-6-1-2.
no_clue: Four digits. Ines's letter says only Tobi would know.
title: INES'S VAULT
prompt: Four dials. The day they met.
explanation: She trusted someone to come back. Someone did.

title: THE WATER CYCLE
prompt: Ines's teaching board: match each step to its name.
explanation: The water you drink has been rain, river, cloud and sea. Whatever we put in it comes back round.
